metadata.title: The Memory Dealer
metadata.description: You awaken in a neon-lit back-room clinic in Neo-Shanghai, 2087. A black-market memory dealer botched an extraction and left you with fragments of stolen memories — including evidence of his operation. He needs to finish the job before you can tell anyone. Escape before Lao Chen erases you completely.
metadata.author: ai-generated

setting.ambient_text: Neon bleeds through fogged plexi-glass. A neural rig hums beside the gurney you woke on. Your skull throbs where electrodes were attached. Somewhere beyond the partition, someone is humming a Cantonese lullaby.

views.back_label: Step back from the neural interface
Step back from the storage rack

items.name: Surgical Scalpel
items.description: A nano-edged scalpel. Standard issue for neural extraction clinics.

then.text: Mono-molecular edge. Could cut through surgical-grade restraints — or just about anything thinner than steel.

items.name: Neural Electrode Patch
items.description: A sticky electrode with trailing wires. Still warm from your skin.

then.text: Model NX-7 transcranial patch. The serial number is scratched off — black market hardware. A small QR code remains readable: 'Lot 4471-C'.
The adhesive is still tacky. Could stick to another surface — or another person's temple.

items.name: Cracked Data Shard
items.description: A translucent memory storage crystal with a hairline fracture.

then.text: Light refracts through the crack, projecting faint holographic numbers on your palm: 7-2-0-4. A memory address? A code? The fragment of someone else's knowledge burns in your mind.
The holographic projection still reads 7-2-0-4.

items.name: Sedative Vial
items.description: A small glass vial of clear liquid. Label reads 'Somnol-X — Neural Suppressant'.

then.text: Fast-acting neural suppressant. Used to keep extraction subjects docile. 10cc would put someone out for hours.

items.name: Clinic Access Card
items.description: A scratched keycard with a faded holographic strip.

then.text: Registered to 'Chen Memory Services — Est. 2081'. The holographic strip still functions. Below, in tiny print: 'Safe override: employee birthday'.

items.name: Copper Wire Bundle
items.description: A coiled bundle of thin copper wire stripped from medical equipment.

then.text: About two meters of thin-gauge copper. Good conductor. Could bridge a circuit or short something out.

items.name: Memory Cartridge (Yours)
items.description: A cylindrical cartridge glowing faintly blue. Your stolen memories are inside.

then.text: Label reads 'SUBJ-4471-C — PARTIAL EXTRACTION — DO NOT SELL'. The glow is your neural pattern. Your identity, bottled.
It's warm to the touch. You feel a strange vertigo holding your own memories in your hand.

items.name: Ledger Photograph
items.description: A holoprint of a ledger page showing names, dates, and prices.

then.text: Dozens of names. Extraction dates. Buyer names. Prices in crypto-yuan. This is irrefutable evidence of Chen's operation. A stolen memory surfaces: a birthday party, August 8, 2039. Chen blowing out candles. The number 0808.

items.name: Encrypted Backup Drive
items.description: A thumb-sized solid-state drive with military-grade encryption.

then.text: Contains Chen's complete client database. Encrypted, but the encryption terminal on the rack could crack it with the right key.

items.name: Modified Neural Headset
items.description: Chen's extraction headset, rewired to transmit instead of receive.

then.text: You reversed the polarity on the neural transceiver. Instead of extracting memories, it will overwrite them. One use — the coils will burn out.

items.name: Pipe Wrench
items.description: A heavy adjustable wrench, caked in rust.

then.text: Standard pipe wrench. Could loosen bolts, pipes, or grates.

items.name: Electric Tea Kettle
items.description: A battered electric kettle. Still warm. Chen's personal comfort in this sterile place.

then.text: Half-full of jasmine tea. Steam curls from the spout. Chen drinks constantly — you can hear him sipping between hums.

items.name: Sedative-Laced Tea Kettle
items.description: The tea kettle, now dosed with fast-acting neural suppressant.

then.text: The sedative dissolved cleanly. No discoloration, no odor over the jasmine. Next time Chen takes a sip...

items.name: Neon Tube
items.description: A salvaged neon tube, still flickering with residual charge.

then.text: Gas-discharge tube. Still has enough charge to arc if shorted. Could overload a small electronic device — or create a convincing distraction.

items.name: Neural Data Cable
items.description: A shielded cable designed to carry neural signals between extraction hardware.

then.text: Shielded NX-series data cable. Standard connector for neural extraction hardware. Could be spliced with the electrode patch to reverse the signal flow.

items.name: Compiled Evidence Package
items.description: A data package containing the ledger, decrypted client database, and your extraction records.

then.text: Everything needed to put Chen away for decades. Client names, extraction logs, financial records. Enough to dismantle the entire black-market memory trade in Neo-Shanghai's District 7.

combinations.message: You pour the sedative into the jasmine tea. It dissolves instantly. A trap fit for a dealer.
You wind copper wire around the neon tube's contacts, creating a crude short-circuit device. Touch it to any electronic panel and watch the sparks fly.
You splice the electrode's transceiver into the data cable and reverse the signal flow. Instead of reading neural patterns, it will write them. A memory overwriter.
You compile the photographic evidence with the decrypted database into a single broadcastable data package. This is enough to bring down Chen's entire network.

objects.name: Medical Gurney
objects.description: A stained surgical gurney with leather restraint straps.

then.text: You're strapped to a medical gurney. Leather restraints on both wrists, buckled tight. The leather is old, cracked at the edges. A tray beside you holds surgical instruments — just out of reach.
The gurney where you woke. Cut restraints dangle from the rails. The instrument tray is empty now.
You twist against the straps. The leather creaks but holds. You need something to cut them — and the instrument tray is inches beyond your fingertips.

messages: You whisper to yourself: 'Think. Think. How did I get here?'
Fragments surface: a bar, a drink, waking here. Someone drugged you.
You mutter: 'The tray. If I could just reach the tray...'

then.text: You saw through the leather restraints with the scalpel. They part with a whisper. You sit up, head swimming, and swing your legs off the gurney. Free.
You can't take a gurney you're strapped to.

objects.name: Instrument Tray
objects.description: A steel surgical tray on a wheeled stand, just out of arm's reach from the gurney.

then.text: A steel tray on a wheeled stand, just inches beyond your fingertips. Scalpels, hemostats, retractors — and one nano-edged surgical scalpel that could slice through these restraints. If only you could reach it.
The instrument tray, now in reach after your desperate rocking. Most of the tools are useless to you, but the scalpel was all you needed.
You strain against the restraints, fingers stretching toward the tray. So close. If you rocked the gurney sideways, the wheels might roll you close enough...
You already grabbed the scalpel. Time to cut yourself free.

You throw your weight sideways. The gurney rocks on its wheels, rolling an inch closer. Again. The leather restraints bite into your wrists. One more heave — the gurney lurches and your fingertips brush the tray's edge. You hook the scalpel's handle and drag it toward you.
Nothing else on the tray is useful enough to pocket.

objects.name: Neural Extraction Rig
objects.description: A hulking machine beside the gurney. Screens dark, fans still spinning.

then.text: A Koryo-Tek MR-9 Neural Extraction Rig. Military surplus, heavily modified. The display shows 'EXTRACTION INTERRUPTED — SUBJECT NEURAL PATTERN: 47% CAPTURED'. You can't reach the controls from the gurney.
The rig's status screen blinks: '47% CAPTURED — RESUME EXTRACTION Y/N?' A closeup view of the neural interface might reveal more.
You lean in to examine the neural interface controls more closely.
You strain toward the rig but the restraints hold you back. Too far.

objects.name: Plastic Partition Curtain
objects.description: A translucent plastic curtain dividing the clinic. Shadows move behind it.

then.text: Thick translucent plastic, the kind used in industrial clean rooms. Through it you can see the blue-white glow of Chen's workstation. His silhouette moves occasionally.
You part the curtain an inch and peer through. Chen's workspace: monitors showing neural patterns, a tea kettle, and a security panel by the exit door. You let the curtain fall back.
You can't reach the curtain from the gurney.

You press your ear to the plastic. Chen is muttering: '...forty-seven percent. Enough to sell the motor skills, maybe the language centers. The episodic? Damaged. Huílái zài shuō...' He trails off, humming.

objects.name: Medicine Cabinet
objects.description: A wall-mounted steel cabinet with a digital lock.

then.text: Steel cabinet, bolted to the wall. Through the glass front you can see vials, syringes, and a small wrench. The digital lock shows 4 zeros.
Locked tight. The digital lock needs a 4-digit code.
Already open. The remaining vials rattle on the shelf.
The scalpel is sharp but the cabinet is steel. You'd need the code or brute force.

objects.name: Floor Drain
objects.description: A steel drain grate set into the tiled floor. Dark stains around the edges.

then.text: A heavy drain grate. Through the gaps you can see a pipe wide enough to crawl through — it slopes downward into darkness. The bolts holding the grate are corroded.
You pull at the grate. The bolts are rusted but still solid. You'd need a wrench.

The bolts scream as they turn. The grate lifts away revealing a drainage pipe — wide enough to crawl through. It slopes down toward the building's sewage system. A way out, if you don't mind the dark.
The pipe descends into blackness. Stale water echoes below. This is a one-way trip — once you drop in, there's no climbing back.

objects.name: Ventilation Grate
objects.description: A ceiling-mounted ventilation grate. Cool air whispers through the slats.

then.text: Industrial ventilation. The duct behind it looks wide enough to crawl through — these old buildings were built for heavy air circulation. Four screws hold it in place.
Too high to reach from the floor, and the screws need a tool anyway.
You climb on the gurney and use the scalpel tip to turn the screws. They come loose one by one. The grate swings open.

objects.name: Neon Sign
objects.description: A wall-mounted neon sign reading '記憶' (Memory) in flickering magenta.

then.text: '記憶' — Memory. The neon tubes pulse with a low electrical hum. The wiring runs exposed along the wall to a junction box.
The tube is hot to the touch and buzzing with voltage. You could remove it, but it would be loud and dark afterward.
You wrench the neon tube free from its mount. The sign goes dark. A faint crackle of residual charge runs along the tube.
Empty mounting brackets where the neon tube was. The corner of the room is noticeably darker now.

objects.name: Security Camera
objects.description: A dome camera mounted in the ceiling corner, red LED blinking.

then.text: A dome camera. The red LED blinks steadily — it's recording. Chen is watching from the other side of the partition. Every move you make, he sees.
The camera's LED blinks green now — it's playing a looped feed of you lying on the gurney. Chen sees nothing.
Mounted too high on the ceiling. You can't reach it, and smashing it would just alert Chen.
You touch the charged neon tube to the camera's power cable. Sparks fly. The camera fries — but now Chen knows something is wrong. A direct approach, not a subtle one.

objects.name: Clinic Exit Door
objects.description: A reinforced steel door with a biometric scanner and keypad.

then.text: Heavy steel door. The only way out of the clinic proper. A biometric scanner glows red beside it, and a keypad beneath that. Through the narrow window you can see a hallway — and beyond that, the street.
Locked. The biometric scanner rejects your palm print. You'd need Chen's access card or the keypad code.
You swipe the card. The scanner turns green — but the keypad flashes, demanding a code too. Dual authentication.

then.reason: You push through the exit door into the neon-soaked alley. The evidence package in your pocket contains everything needed to dismantle Chen's operation. You disappear into the rain-slicked streets of Neo-Shanghai, already composing the encrypted message to the Cyber Crimes Division. Chen won't be selling anyone else's memories.

else.reason: You push through the exit door and stumble into the neon-soaked alley. Free. Alive. But without evidence, Chen will just relocate and start again. You escaped — but the memory trade continues.

objects.name: Biometric Security Panel
objects.description: The dual-authentication panel beside the exit door.

then.text: Dual-auth security panel. Slot for access card on top, 4-digit keypad below. Both must be satisfied to unlock the exit.
The panel buzzes angrily. Access denied.

objects.name: Supply Shelf
objects.description: Metal shelving unit stacked with medical supplies and electronic components.

then.text: Cluttered shelves of medical supplies: gauze, syringes, antiseptic. Between the shelves, bundles of copper wire stripped for recycling. The shelf is large enough to hide behind in a pinch.
You rummage through the supplies. Mostly standard clinic stock. You pocket a bundle of copper wire — could be useful.
The shelf is bolted to the wall. You grab the copper wire instead.

objects.name: Medical Waste Bin
objects.description: A dented metal waste bin marked with a biohazard symbol.

then.text: Biohazard waste bin. Through the opening you can see discarded electrode patches, used syringes, and... a cracked data shard, glinting under the neon light.
You reach into the waste. Past the used patches and broken syringes, your fingers close around a cracked data shard. Someone's discarded memories — or part of yours?
Nothing else worth salvaging. Just medical waste.

objects.name: Power Junction Box
objects.description: An exposed junction box where the clinic's power lines converge.

then.text: A rats-nest of power cables. Three main circuits are labeled: 'EXTRACTION RIG', 'SECURITY/CAMERAS', and 'COOLING SYSTEM'. A toggle panel controls which circuits receive power.
The circuits are controlled by the toggle panel. Flipping them by hand would risk electrocution.

You jam the charged neon tube into the junction box. A cascade of sparks erupts and the lights flicker violently. The power grid destabilizes — the entire building goes dark for a moment before emergency lighting kicks in. On the other side of the curtain, Chen curses.

objects.name: Intercom Speaker
objects.description: A wall-mounted intercom unit. Chen uses it to talk to clients in the waiting room.

then.text: A two-way intercom. The 'BROADCAST' toggle is off. If turned on, it transmits to the building's public address system — every unit in this floor of the building would hear.
You flip the broadcast toggle. The intercom crackles to life. A faint hum indicates it's now transmitting to the building PA.

You hold the evidence package's data output to the intercom microphone. The building PA crackles as names, dates, and transaction records broadcast to every unit on this floor. Chen's neighbors — many of them his clients — hear everything. You hear Chen scream from the other side of the curtain. It's over for him.
"If anyone can hear me — I'm being held captive in unit 7B! Lao Chen is running an illegal memory extraction operation! Someone call the PSB!" Your voice echoes through the building.

objects.name: Ceiling Pipes
objects.description: Exposed industrial pipes running across the ceiling. One is dripping.

then.text: Exposed water and coolant pipes. One has a slow drip. The pipe nearest the ventilation grate has a loose coupling — a wrench could loosen it further.
You loosen the coupling on the water pipe. Water begins to spray in a steady stream, pooling on the floor. The sound of running water fills the room — perfect cover for other noises.
Water sprays from the loosened coupling, filling the room with the sound of rushing water. Good cover noise — your movements will be harder to hear.

objects.name: Extraction Chair
objects.description: A reclining chair surrounded by neural interface equipment. The headset sits in a cradle.

then.text: The extraction chair. This is where Chen sits his subjects. The neural headset rests in a cradle beside it, trailing cables to the main rig. A calibration panel with dials controls the extraction parameters.
You sit in the chair experimentally. The neural headset cradle is within reach, and the calibration dials are right beside you.

objects.name: Neural Headset Cradle
objects.description: A padded cradle holding Chen's neural extraction headset.

then.text: Chen's neural extraction headset. A crown of electrodes and transceivers designed to read and copy neural patterns. With the right modifications, the signal flow could be reversed — instead of extracting memories, it would overwrite them.
You lift the headset from the cradle. It's lighter than expected — mostly circuitry. You'll need to combine it with the right components to reverse its function.
Empty cradle. You took the headset.

objects.name: Neural Activity Display
objects.description: A holographic display showing real-time neural pattern analysis.

then.text: The display shows your neural pattern — fragmented, gaps where memories were extracted. The interface reads: 'SUBJECT 4471-C — 47% EXTRACTED — PATTERN UNSTABLE'. A data cable port glows on the side of the display unit.
You tap through the menus. Patient history, extraction logs, calibration settings. One menu reads 'SECURITY FEED OVERRIDE' — but it's password protected.

You swipe Chen's access card through the display's reader. The security menu unlocks. You navigate to 'CAMERA FEED OVERRIDE' and set the security camera to loop its last 60 seconds of footage. The camera LED shifts from red to green — Chen now sees an empty gurney on his monitors.

objects.name: Memory Cartridge Slot
objects.description: A slot in the extraction rig where memory cartridges are loaded for reading or writing.

then.text: An empty cartridge slot. Memory cartridges from the storage rack would fit here. Loading one would let you access its contents on the neural display.

You slide your memory cartridge into the slot. The display flares to life with your own neural pattern — fragmented, incomplete, but recognizable. Your memories. Partially restored, the gaps become clearer. One fragment surfaces: a view of Chen's safe, the combination being entered: 0-8-0-8.

objects.name: Calibration Dials
objects.description: A panel of precision dials controlling the neural extraction parameters.

then.text: Three precision dials: FREQUENCY (MHz), AMPLITUDE (mV), and PHASE OFFSET (degrees). Currently set to extraction parameters. A frequency tuning dial could be recalibrated to broadcast on the district emergency channel.
You could adjust the dials, but without knowing the correct emergency broadcast frequency, you'd just be sending noise.

You set the frequency dial to 108.7 MHz — the district emergency channel. The rig's neural transmitter is now repurposed as a broadcast antenna. If you had compiled evidence, you could broadcast it to every receiver in the district.

objects.name: Data Cable
objects.description: A thick data cable trailing from the extraction rig to the headset cradle.

then.text: A shielded neural data cable. Carries signals between the headset and the extraction rig. The connector is standard NX-series — it could interface with the electrode patch.
You disconnect the data cable from the rig and coil it up. Could be spliced with other neural components.

objects.name: Patient Records Terminal
objects.description: A terminal showing Chen's patient database.

then.text: Login screen. 'CHEN MEMORY SERVICES — PATIENT DATABASE'. Requires access card authentication.

The card reader accepts Chen's credentials. The database opens: hundreds of patient records. Extraction dates, buyer information, payment records. You scroll to your own file: 'SUBJ-4471-C — STATUS: IN PROGRESS'. Under notes: 'Emergency broadcast frequency for district: 108.7 MHz. Disable before extraction to prevent subject distress calls.' Chen wrote down the very thing you need.

objects.name: Memory Storage Rack
objects.description: A floor-to-ceiling rack of glowing memory cartridges. Hundreds of stolen lives.

then.text: Hundreds of memory cartridges glow in neat rows, each labeled with a subject number. Blues, greens, amber — different memory types. Yours would be here somewhere. The cooling unit hums beside the rack, keeping the cartridges stable.
You scan the labels... 4471-A, 4471-B... there. 4471-C. Your cartridge. You pull it from the rack.

objects.name: Labeled Cartridges
objects.description: Rows of memory cartridges with subject numbers and dates.

then.text: Each cartridge has a subject number, extraction date, and buyer code. Some are marked 'SOLD'. Others: 'PENDING'. A few are red-tagged: 'CORRUPTED — DO NOT SELL'. The dates go back six years.

You read the labels aloud, barely whispering. 'Subject 3102... extracted 2084-03-15... sold to buyer KZ-7 for 45,000 crypto-yuan.' Six years of stolen lives, organized like inventory. Hundreds of people who woke up not knowing who they were.

objects.name: Cooling Unit
objects.description: An industrial cooling unit keeping the memory cartridges at optimal temperature.

then.text: Industrial coolant system keeping the memory cartridges at -12°C. If it stopped, the cartridges would begin degrading within minutes. Chen's entire inventory — years of work — would be destroyed.
The power cable is thick and reinforced. You'd need to cut the power at the junction box to disable it.

objects.name: Inventory Ledger
objects.description: A physical notebook — old-school record-keeping in a digital age.

then.text: A worn leather notebook. Chen keeps paper records as backup — smart, in an age where digital evidence can be wiped remotely.

You flip through pages of meticulous handwriting. Names, dates, amounts. Every extraction Chen has ever performed. You photograph a key page with the data shard's holographic function — this is hard evidence.

objects.name: Encryption Terminal
objects.description: A standalone terminal used to encrypt and decrypt memory data.

then.text: Chen's encryption workstation. Used to encrypt memory cartridges before sale. The decrypt function requires a physical drive to be inserted.

You insert the backup drive. The terminal whirs to life: 'DECRYPTING... KEY FOUND IN LOCAL KEYSTORE... COMPLETE.' The drive's contents are now readable. Client names, transaction records, extraction schedules — Chen's entire black market operation, decrypted.

objects.name: Backup Drive Slot
objects.description: A small drive bay with a blinking status LED.

then.text: A thumb-sized solid-state drive sits in the bay, its LED blinking amber. Chen's encrypted backup of his entire client database.
You pop the drive from its bay. Encrypted, but the encryption terminal nearby could crack it.

objects.name: Chen's Personal Safe
objects.description: A small wall-mounted safe with a 4-digit combination lock.

then.text: A compact wall safe with a 4-digit combination lock. Chen's personal valuables. The access card mentioned 'employee birthday' as the safe override.
The combination lock resists. You need a 4-digit code.
The safe is empty now — you took the access card and tea kettle.

on_solve.text: The keypad beeps. 7-2-0-4. The code from the cracked data shard — a memory that isn't yours, but saved your life. The exit door's magnetic lock disengages with a heavy thunk.

on_fail.text: Wrong code. The panel flashes red.

on_solve.text: 0-8-0-8. August 8th. Chen's birthday — the stolen memory gave you that. The safe clicks open. Inside: Chen's personal access card and his battered tea kettle, still warm.

on_fail.text: Wrong combination. The dials click uselessly.

on_solve.text: You reroute all power to the extraction rig, cutting security cameras and the cooling system. The camera LED goes dark. The cooling unit whines down to silence. Without cooling, the memory cartridges will begin to degrade — Chen's entire inventory is at risk. But the neural rig now has full power for a broadcast.

on_fail.text: The toggles click but nothing useful happens. The current configuration doesn't help.

on_solve.text: The cabinet clicks open. Inside: vials of sedative, a pipe wrench, and surgical supplies. You grab the sedative and the wrench.

phases.name: Disoriented

on_enter.text: Your skull throbs. Electrodes dangle from your temples. You're strapped to a gurney in a neon-lit room that smells of antiseptic and ozone. Someone is humming behind a plastic curtain.

phases.ambient_text: Neon hum. Distant humming. The drip of coolant.

phases.name: Recovering

on_enter.text: Free from the gurney. Your legs shake. Fragments of stolen memories flash behind your eyes — faces you don't recognize, places you've never been. You need to focus. Find a way out.

phases.ambient_text: The hum of machinery. Chen's occasional muttering beyond the curtain.

phases.name: Lucid

on_enter.text: The stolen memories are crystallizing. You can feel them integrating — someone else's knowledge becoming yours. Chen's operation, his clients, his methods. You know enough now. The question is what to do with it.

phases.ambient_text: Tension thick as smoke. Every sound from beyond the curtain is a threat.

effects.text: A memory that isn't yours surfaces: a woman's face, terrified, begging. 'Please, I have children—' Then static. Someone else's nightmare, lodged in your brain.

Chen's phone rings beyond the curtain. You hear his side: 'Wèi? ...Yes, the new subject. Partial extraction. Forty-seven percent... No, still viable. Motor skills, some language centers... Thirty thousand? For partial? Nǐ zài shuō xiào ba... Fifty, minimum. I'll have it ready by morning.' He hangs up.

The lights flicker. The whole district's power grid is unstable tonight — Neo-Shanghai's infrastructure crumbling under the weight of illegal power taps. Chen curses from the other room: 'Gāisǐ de power grid... if I lose another cartridge batch...'
A buzzer sounds. Chen's voice, muffled: 'You're early. Wait in the hall.' The building's front door opens and closes. A client — here to buy your memories. The clock just got shorter.

An alarm blares from the storage rack. 'THERMAL WARNING — CARTRIDGE DEGRADATION IN PROGRESS.' Chen screams from beyond the curtain: 'THE COOLING! WHAT HAPPENED TO THE COOLING?!' You hear frantic footsteps — he's panicking about his inventory.

killer.name: Lao Chen
killer.description: A black-market memory dealer in his sixties. Precise, businesslike, philosophical. He sees memories as commodities — nothing personal. He hums Cantonese lullabies while he works and drinks jasmine tea constantly. He is genuinely curious about the nature of identity and consciousness, which makes his crimes all the more chilling.

on_approach: Time to check on our guest... the neural patterns should be stabilizing.
Hm. Let me see how the extraction is progressing.
The buyer wants proof of quality. Let me take a look...
on_search: Interesting. The gurney is empty. Where did you go, 4471-C?
Don't make this difficult. A struggling subject damages the neural pattern — lowers the resale value.
I can hear you breathing, you know. These walls are thin.
Zhǎo dào nǐ le... I always find them.
on_clear: Still resting. Good. The extraction will resume shortly.
Neural patterns stable. Excellent quality — the buyer will be pleased.
on_evidence: The restraints are cut? Clever. But this clinic has no exits you can reach.
You've been busy. That's a shame — struggling degrades the memory quality. Ruins the product.
My safe? You found my safe. How very... resourceful. Pity it won't help you.
The cooling system? Do you have any idea what those cartridges are worth? Bèn dàn!
on_catch: There you are. Don't worry — the second extraction is always smoother. You won't remember any of this.
Caught. Sit down, 4471-C. We have a buyer waiting, and I don't like to keep clients waiting. Bù hǎo yìsi — nothing personal.

effects.text: Chen notices the open ventilation grate. He drags a heavy equipment cart under it, blocking the duct. 'Nice try. But I've had runners before.'
Chen spots the active intercom and yanks the broadcast toggle off. 'Broadcasting? In MY clinic? You're more trouble than you're worth, 4471-C.'

special_behaviors.description: Chen is occupied — phone call, panicking about cooling, or dealing with a client.

win_conditions.description: Escape through the front door with compiled evidence
Broadcast evidence on the emergency frequency
Use the modified headset to overwrite Chen's memories

lose_conditions.description: Chen finds you during a search
Chen's client arrives and the extraction resumes

hints.text: You're strapped to the gurney. Look around — there might be something within reach to cut yourself free.
The instrument tray beside the gurney has surgical tools. Try to reach it by rocking the gurney.
That security camera is watching everything you do. Find a way to disable or loop its feed before moving freely.
The access card mentioned Chen's birthday as the safe override. A stolen memory might surface with that information...
The ledger in the storage area and the encrypted backup drive together would make a powerful evidence package.
The cracked data shard in the waste bin might hold useful information. Examine it closely.
The floor drain is wide enough to crawl through, but the bolts need a wrench. Check the medicine cabinet.
Chen drinks tea constantly. If you had a sedative and his tea kettle...
The neural rig could be repurposed as a broadcast antenna if you knew the emergency frequency. Check patient records.
The neural headset extracts memories. With the right components, you could reverse it to write memories instead. The electrode patch and data cable might work...

solution_paths.name: The Whistleblower
solution_paths.description: Compile evidence of Chen's operation and escape through the front door to deliver it to authorities.
steps: Free yourself from the gurney using the scalpel (rock gurney → look at tray → take scalpel → hand on gurney)
Loop the security camera feed (find access card → use on neural display in neural_closeup)
Obtain access card from Chen's safe (examine ledger → get birthday memory → crack safe combination 0808)
Get the exit door keypad code (find data shard in waste bin → examine it → learn code 7204)
Compile evidence (photograph ledger + decrypt backup drive → combine into evidence package)
Unlock exit door (swipe access card + enter keypad code 7204)
Walk out with evidence package

solution_paths.name: The Rat
solution_paths.description: Escape through the floor drain into the building's sewage system. Quick but you leave without evidence.
steps: Free yourself from the gurney
Get wrench from medicine cabinet (need safe code 0808 for cabinet keypad)
Use wrench on floor drain to remove grate (very loud — 30 noise)
Drop into the drain pipe and crawl to freedom

solution_paths.name: The Signal
solution_paths.description: Repurpose the neural extraction rig as a broadcast antenna and transmit evidence on the emergency frequency.
steps: Free yourself from the gurney
Access patient records terminal (get access card → use on terminal → learn frequency 108.7 MHz)
Reroute power to extraction rig (toggle panel: rig ON, security OFF, cooling OFF)
Set calibration dials to emergency frequency
Compile evidence package (ledger photo + decrypted backup drive)
Broadcast evidence through the rig (evidence package becomes broadcast — Chen's operation exposed)
Optional: escape through now-unmonitored exit or drain while Chen panics

solution_paths.name: The Eraser
solution_paths.description: Modify the neural headset to overwrite memories instead of extracting them. Use it on Chen — make him forget you exist.
steps: Free yourself from the gurney
Take the electrode patch from the headset cradle (neural_closeup)
Take the data cable from the extraction rig (neural_closeup)
